Hey Ben,

Thanks for the note and the proposed time — appreciate the compact approach. Quick update from my side: our CIO (Michael Cruz) is traveling Apr 23–26 and won't be available for a live walkthrough. The VP of Cloud Engineering (Elena) can join for a 30-minute slot on Apr 25 between 13:00–15:30 PT. If the CIO can join asynchronously for a 10-minute live Q&A, that could work, otherwise we may need to record and surface the key points.

Can your team run a 30-minute leadership-focused demo that zeroes in on:
- 10 min: high-level run-of-show (value, deployment options, SLAs)
- 12 min: short live demo (latency/cost comparison + routing policy example)
- 8 min: questions + next steps (procurement & pilot milestones)

Also, procurement will want an itemized list of what to expect from a pilot (SLA targets, data residency options, logging/audit access). Appreciate if you can include that.

Thanks,
Samir

Samir — great, thanks for the clarity. Apr 25 13:30 PT works on our side for a 30-minute leadership session. We'll aim to keep it tight to the timings you outlined.

Quick plan who does what:
- Ben: 3–4 minute intros and outcomes/next-steps framing + procurement handoff
- Marissa (SE): 12-minute targeted demo showing request routing, cost trade-offs, and a live example of automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant
- Jonas (Customer Success): 8-minute pilot milestones, metrics we monitor (latency P95, token cost, cache hit %), and documentation/access cadence

We will prepare a one-page pilot checklist for procurement and attach it to the calendar invite. I am attaching a compact agenda and a CTO-facing tech brief for Michael in case he wants to scan before/after the session. If Michael can jump on for the final 10 minutes, perfect — if not we will record and send a timestamped highlight reel targeting the procurement questions.

Proposed calendar hold: Apr 25, 2029 13:30–14:00 PT (30 min) — I will send shortly.

Best,

Hi Samir / team —

Thanks — I updated the demo flow to be ultra-targeted for a leadership audience and included a short procurement appendix. A couple of operational notes I wanted to surface before we lock the invite:

1) Live demo scope: I'll demo two configurations in <5 min each — (a) Hosted API (fastest time-to-value) and (b) Dedicated pool with autoscaling (predictable throughput). I'll show a sequence of the same prompt across both to illustrate latency and cost delta.

2) Telemetry & evidence: for procurement I'm ready to show token-level cost breakdown and a sample audit log (redacted) for retention policy. If you need SOC2 artifacts during the meeting, flag it and I'll ask CS to have SOC2 summary on hand.

3) Recording & highlight reel: we'll record; if Michael can't join live we'll extract 3 clips: 00:00–03:30 (value framing), 06:30–11:00 (demo contrast), 23:30–30:00 (procurement Q&A).

4) Pre-reads: attaching the compact agenda and a 1-page pilot checklist so procurement can jump straight to milestones and acceptance criteria.

If Apr 25 13:30–14:00 PT is good, please accept the invite when Ben sends it.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Key logistics and asks:
- Please share any procurement stakeholders who should be on the invite (legal, procurement), or reply-all with their contact info and we'll add a short procurement pre-brief.
